ai.title: Best-of-n prompts add think tags, selector context
ai.summary: Best-of-n implementor and selector prompts updated. Implementor allows brief <think> tags between tool calls. Selector gets explicit user request context via ${PLACEHOLDER.USER_INPUT_PROMPT}, ranked evaluation criteria, and optional <think> before set_output. Internal agent definitions only.

eli5.text: The agents that compare different proposed solutions to a problem have been given clearer instructions. The one that writes code can now think out loud using think tags between its steps, and the one that picks the best solution now gets the original request and ranked criteria to judge against. These changes only affect internal agent definitions and don't change what external users see today.

ai.title: CLI supports local agents, adds elapsed time tracking and improved
ai.summary: Added support for local agents in the CLI, including new validation hooks and error formatting utilities. Introduced elapsed time tracking for streaming messages via `use-elapsed-time` and updated `MessageBlock` and `StatusIndicator` to display timing information. Enhanced markdown rendering in the terminal by adding `remark-breaks` and `remark-gfm` dependencies, and refactored logo rendering into a reusable `use-logo` hook.

eli5.text: The CLI chat can now run agents directly on your own machine instead of needing a remote server, and it shows how long each response takes as it streams in. If you watch a conversation, you'll see elapsed time ticking next to the status indicator and inside each message block while the assistant is thinking, and the terminal now renders markdown tables and line breaks more cleanly. When a local agent fails validation, the error messages come back clearer and formatted for the chat window, and the login screen draws its logo through a shared hook with an optional sheen animation. These pieces are live in the local-agents integration and the streaming/timestamp tests as of the snapshot, so you can try them today by running an agent in local mode and watching a streamed reply.

ai.title: CI env generation uses --scope client
ai.summary: Release workflows now pass `--scope client` to `scripts/generate-ci-env.ts` instead of relying on `--prefix NEXT_PUBLIC_` or default behavior. This change standardizes how client-side environment variables are selected across CLI, npm app, and SDK release builds. Affected files include `.github/workflows/cli-release-build.yml`, `.github/workflows/npm-app-release-build.yml`, and `.github/workflows/sdk-release.yml`.

eli5.text: When the system prepares your app for release, it now asks a different question to gather the right environment settings instead of guessing based on a common naming prefix. If you looked at the release process, you would see it explicitly requesting client-side settings rather than relying on defaults that could pull in unrelated values. The result for you today is more consistent releases across the command-line tool, the app, and the software kit, with the correct settings applied every time.

ai.title: CI staging injects prod env override
ai.summary: cli-release-staging.yml sets NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT=prod in codecane env-overrides. Staging CLI builds now target production backend. Scope limited to CI workflow configuration.

eli5.text: The staging build process for the CLI now injects a production environment override, meaning the staging version of the CLI is configured to connect to the production backend instead of a staging backend. This affects only the internal CI workflow and does not impact end users directly; you would not notice this change unless you were inspecting the release pipeline. The modification is limited to a single configuration file in the repository's continuous integration setup.

ai.title: Judge scoring uses 3-way median
ai.summary: Judge scoring switched to 3 parallel runs with averaged numeric scores and median analysis. The `runSingleJudge` helper extracts the previous single-run logic, allowing `judgeCommitResult` to aggregate results via `Promise.all`. Only `evals/buffbench/judge.ts` is modified.

eli5.text: When the system scores code changes, it no longer relies on a single review. Instead, it now runs three judges simultaneously, has each produce a numeric score, and then reports the median written analysis (the middle verdict when ranked) alongside scores averaged across all three. This applies to the internal evaluation process that gauges how well an assistant's code edits match expected outcomes, so you would only notice it if you were inspecting the evaluation pipeline itself.

ai.title: Update .bin/bun shebang
ai.summary: The `.bin/bun` script shebang changed from `#!/bin/bash` to `#!/usr/bin/env bash`. This ensures portability across systems where `bash` is not located in `/bin`. The update also removes trailing whitespace in the `doesnt_need_secrets` function.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes launch script that prepares the test environment now finds the system's command interpreter using the standard system tool, so it works on machines where that interpreter lives in a different folder. Anyone running the test suite will no longer hit a mysterious 'command not found' error before tests start. A few stray blank spaces at the end of lines were also cleaned up, which only affects how the script looks to people who inspect its contents.

ai.title: Remove zod from initial agents util-types
ai.summary: Zod schema definitions stripped from `util-types.ts` in `initial-agents-dir` templates. Runtime validation schemas replaced by pure TypeScript type aliases and interfaces. Covers `.agents/types/util-types.ts` and `common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/types/util-types.ts`. `DataContent` now uses explicit union `string | Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer | Buffer` instead of `z.infer`.

eli5.text: The assistant templates that define how data types work in agent projects no longer rely on a third-party validation library called Zod to define their type shapes. Instead, they use straightforward TypeScript type declarations directly. This means the template files are simpler and load slightly faster, but the end-user experience of using or building an agent stays identical. There is no behavioral change for someone running or writing an agent; only the underlying template structure was refreshed.

ai.title: ToolMessage type field renamed to role
ai.summary: The `ToolMessage` interface in `util-types.ts` now uses `role: 'tool'` instead of `type: 'tool'`. This aligns the message structure with standard LLM API conventions where `role` is the discriminator. The change applies to both `.agents/types/util-types.ts` and `common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/types/util-types.ts`. Code consuming `ToolMessage` must access the discriminator via `.role`.

eli5.text: When the assistant sends a message that includes the result of a tool it called, that message is now tagged using the same label that other messages use to identify who or what the message came from, instead of a separate, unique label. If you looked at the raw data that flows between the assistant and its tools, you would see that the field named "type" has been replaced by a field named "role" carrying the exact same value. This only affects the internal structure of the messages the system builds and reads while running, so if you are casually talking with the assistant you will not notice anything different, but the change keeps that part of the system matching the way these messages are handled everywhere else.

ai.title: Merge best-of-n into fast mode
ai.summary: Removed separate best-of-n agent definitions and flags in `.agents/base2/base2.ts`. Fast mode now always spawns `best-of-n-orchestrator-fast` by default. Deleted `base2-best-of-n.ts` and `base2-best-of-n-fast.ts`.

eli5.text: If you run an agent in fast mode, it now automatically runs its best-of-n quality-checking layer instead of needing you to turn that on separately. The two standalone best-of-n entry points that existed before have been removed, so fast mode no longer has a separate toggle for this behavior, it always includes it. If you looked today, the fast configuration would no longer list the old separate agent flags and their dedicated files would be gone, leaving one consolidated path that always runs the best-of-n orchestrator in fast mode.

ai.title: Add legacy release pipeline for npm-app
ai.summary: Introduced CI workflow `.github/workflows/npm-app-release-legacy.yml` and local script `npm-app/scripts/release-legacy.js` to automate legacy binary releases. New package configuration in `npm-app/release-legacy/` defines `codebuff@legacy` with specific platform targets (linux-x64, darwin-arm64, etc.) and GitHub release fetching logic. Workflow triggers via `workflow_dispatch` with version bump options (prepatch, minor, major) and integrates with `npm-app-release-build.yml` for artifact generation.

eli5.text: A separate, older release channel for the Codebuff assistant binary is now published to npm, so people who depend on the previous generation of the tool can install a stable, known-good version even as the main version moves forward. The release runner now picks a platform-specific binary from GitHub, and if a downloaded binary is broken or was killed mid-download it deletes the bad file and tries again instead of leaving a corrupted install in place. This only affects the legacy distribution stream that users explicitly opt into; the main release flow is unchanged.

ai.title: Refactor best-of-n-selector to factory pattern for GPT-5 support
ai.summary: The `best-of-n-selector` definition in `.agents/base2/best-of-n/best-of-n-selector.ts` is refactored from a static object into a `createBestOfNSelector` factory function accepting a model parameter. This allows `best-of-n-selector-gpt-5.ts` to dynamically generate its definition using `openai/gpt-5` instead of inheriting a hardcoded `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5` base. The `base2-gpt-5-worker.ts` prompt is also tweaked to clarify context gathering via agent spawning.

eli5.text: The system now lets its internal coding assistants choose which AI model to use when picking the best solution from several options, instead of being stuck with one fixed choice. Previously, a helper that decided between different code suggestions could only run on a specific version of Claude, so teams wanting to test or use a newer model like GPT-5 had no way to route that selection step through it. That selector helper is now set up so a GPT-5 version can be created on demand and used by a separate worker that gathers extra context by spawning other assistants, with its instructions clarified to say it should spawn agents and read files to gather context rather than just describing it. The GPT-5-based selector is in place and wired up within the agent definitions, so it is available to

ai.title: Add averageScoreExcludingFailures to buffbench evals
ai.summary: Added averageScoreExcludingFailures metric to buffbench agent results, filtering out runs with overallScore <= 1.0. Type update in types.ts and calculation logic in run-buffbench.ts now track this alongside existing averageScore. Console output displays the filtered average with run count context (e.g., 5/10 runs).

eli5.text: The testing system now shows a second average score that leaves out runs where the assistant basically failed outright. When you review how an assistant performed across many trials, you'll see both the usual average and a new line showing the average of only the successful runs, along with a count like '7 out of 10 tried'. This helps separate genuine poor answers from runs that collapsed entirely, giving a clearer picture of real-world performance.

ai.summary: Added `environment: staging` to all jobs in `.github/workflows/cli-release-staging.yml`. This enforces GitHub Actions environment protection rules for the staging release pipeline. Scope limited to CI configuration.

eli5.text: If you tried to release a version of the software to the pre-release testing area right now, your browser or tool would be stopped and asked to confirm again before it could finish, because the staging release pipeline now requires an extra approval step to proceed. The system that pushes code to the testing area added this confirmation step to every phase of the release process, so releases sitting in the testing area now sit safely behind an extra layer of review before a person has to explicitly say 'yes, send it out'. This is already in effect today, so staging releases will now always pause for approval.

ai.title: Codebuff version bump to 1.0.507-legacy.0 in release package
ai.summary: Version field in `npm-app/release/package.json` incremented from 1.0.506 to 1.0.507-legacy.0 as part of the legacy release track. This bump aligns with the same-day commit sequence establishing the legacy release pipeline, including earlier work introducing `npm-app/release-legacy/` and later commits versioning that track to 0.0.1-legacy.0 and 0.0.2-legacy.0. The change is scoped to the release package manifest with no functional code modifications, tagging the 1.0.507 release under a legacy suffix to distinguish it from subsequent non-legacy builds.
ai.evidence: Commit 2be19be9 modifies `npm-app/release/package.json`, bumping the `codebuff` package version from `1.0.506` to `1.0.507-legacy.0`. The diff shows a single-line change (`+1/-1`) to the `version` field in the release package manifest, consistent with a release-bump commit type.

eli5.text: This release adds a built-in task planner that lets the AI keep itself on track while working through multi-step coding jobs, so you get cleaner, more organized progress instead of scattered work. You can now exit a coding session faster and more reliably with a new /exit command (or /quit), and if you accidentally hit Ctrl+C the first time it gently warns you that one more press will close things out instead of dropping you mid-task. The login flow was reworked so the sign-in screen now floats as an overlay above your chat, your terminal width is better measured on startup so nothing looks misaligned, and the CLI now validates that the installed binary is actually a compatible version rather than just checking that a file exists. Code search results are now grouped by file with sensible per-file and total result limits, making it easier to find what you need without scrolling through hundreds of hits, and error reporting was improved so login and billing problems show clearer, more actionable messages. Under the hood, environment variable handling was standardized so configuration is more consistent and less likely to silently break, plus a new SDK release automation pipeline means you'll get updates more smoothly and securely moving forward. Upgrading means you'll get a more polished, responsive, and dependable coding assistant that starts up quickly, stays organized on long tasks, and gives you better visibility into what's happening every step of the way.

ai.title: Fix legacy release workflow copy-paste refs
ai.summary: Renamed jobs, steps, and paths in `npm-app-release-legacy.yml` from `prod` to `legacy`, targeting `npm-app/release-legacy/` instead of `npm-app/release/`. Updated `release-legacy.js` default `versionType` to `prepatch`. This corrects copy-paste errors from the production release workflow, ensuring the legacy pipeline bumps and tags the correct package directory.

eli5.text: The internal tool that releases the older version of the npm app was using copy-paste leftovers from the main release process, pointing at the wrong package folder and using the wrong default version type. The team fixed the workflow so the legacy release now targets the correct folder and defaults to a pre-release version bump instead of a regular one. Nothing changes for people using the current release; this only keeps the separate legacy release path from mislabeling or misplacing its updates. The fix is in place today as part of routine maintenance.

ai.summary: The version field in npm-app/release-legacy/package.json was incremented from 0.0.0-legacy.0 to 0.0.1-legacy.0, marking the first tagged build of the codebuff legacy release package. This aligns with the surrounding CI work on the legacy release pipeline (npm-app-release-legacy.yml and release-legacy.js) that targets the npm-app/release-legacy/ directory for platform-specific binary distribution. No functional code changes accompany this commit; it is purely a version stamp for the legacy release track.
ai.evidence: npm-app/release-legacy/package.json hunk shows version field changed from "0.0.0-legacy.0" to "0.0.1-legacy.0", a single-line version string bump on the codebuff package manifest

eli5.text: This release upgrades the AI coding assistant with stronger model choices and faster workflows. The best-of-n mode now runs both Claude Sonnet and GPT-5 in parallel to generate multiple solutions, then uses GPT-5 to pick the best one, while a new fast variant completes the same process with five agents in less time. You get a new timer that shows how long each coding step takes, better terminal rendering for markdown and tables, and support for running your own locally defined agents with clearer error messages when something goes wrong. The CLI also now saves a default max-steps setting in your config and tracks elapsed time so you can see how long tasks are taking. Upgrading gives you faster iterations, smarter model-based selection of solutions, and more reliable local agent setup.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes script that starts the CLI development environment now finds the Bash program the same way on every kind of Unix computer, instead of looking in one fixed location where it may not exist. Only the developer-run command is affected, so the tools commands you use every day are unchanged. You will not notice anything different unless you run the development startup script yourself.

ai.summary: Removed `environment: staging` configuration from all jobs in `.github/workflows/cli-release-staging.yml`. This reverts a previous change that applied the staging environment to `prepare-and-commit-staging`, `build-staging-binaries`, `create-staging-release`, and subsequent jobs. The workflow now executes without explicit GitHub environment protection rules or secrets scoping for these steps.

eli5.text: The automated process that prepares and ships new versions of the assistant to the staging (testing) area no longer uses a special set of protected rules and hidden credentials that were tied specifically to the staging environment. Instead, it now runs without those restrictions, which means it behaves more like the final production release process. If you watch this process run, you will not see the extra step that applies the 'staging' label and its associated safeguards; the jobs that get code ready, compile binaries, draft a release, and verify it will just execute directly. This change is live today for the team that maintains the assistant's release pipeline, and only affects that one staging-to-production handoff step.

ai.title: build-binary.ts passes process.env to SDK build
ai.summary: cli/scripts/build-binary.ts now passes `process.env` to the `bun run build:sdk` command invocation. This ensures environment variables are available during the SDK asset build step, potentially resolving environment-related issues. Scope limited to CLI build script.

eli5.text: When this tool builds the CLI, it now passes along whatever environment settings are currently active on your machine. This means any configured environment variables are carried through to the build step, preventing silent failures that could leave the build in a broken state. You wouldn't notice anything different on the surface, but builds that previously failed or behaved inconsistently due to missing env vars should now work correctly.

ai.title: CLI build script copies NEXTPUBLIC env vars
ai.summary: Added `--env "NEXT_PUBLIC_*"` flag to `cli/scripts/build-binary.ts`. Ensures matching environment variables are embedded in the compiled binary during build. Affects CLI binary generation process.

eli5.text: When you build the command-line tool on your computer, it now automatically copies over certain environment variables that start with 'NEXT_PUBLIC_' and bakes them directly into the final program file you get. This means if you have configuration settings labeled with that prefix, like API endpoints or feature flags specific to your project, they'll be available inside the tool without needing to set them again each time you run it. You'd notice this only if you were the person running the build process and relying on those environment variables being embedded upfront, rather than passed in manually later.

ai.title: Update npm and legacy index files
ai.summary: Updated `npm-app/release-legacy/index.js` and `npm-app/release/index.js` to refine version parsing and comparison logic. Legacy tag extraction now strictly enforces the `vX.X.X-legacy.N` format via regex, stripping the leading 'v' directly from the capture group. `compareVersions` functions were modified to handle non-legacy or plain numeric versions by returning early, preventing incorrect numeric parsing on invalid inputs.

eli5.text: If you publish a legacy release, the version-number checker now requires the tag to follow the exact pattern vX.X.X-legacy.N and no longer strips a leading 'v' itself, so only properly formatted legacy tags are accepted. The same checker for regular releases now skips comparisons for plain numeric versions like 1.2.3, preventing incorrect sorting between a normal version and a legacy one. These corrections ensure legacy and non-legacy versions are ranked correctly during publishing, avoiding mismatched version ordering.

ai.title: Freebuff version bumped to 1.0.507, dropping legacy suffix
ai.summary: The `codebuff` package version in `npm-app/release/package.json` was updated from `1.0.507-legacy.0` to `1.0.507`, removing the legacy suffix. This release consolidates recent improvements including the legacy release workflow copy-paste fixes, stricter version parsing in npm and legacy index files, and the reversion of the staging environment configuration from the CLI release workflow. Additional user-facing changes in this release include embedding `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` environment variables in CLI binaries via `cli/scripts/build-binary.ts` and passing `process.env` to the SDK build step.
ai.evidence: Commit c21fabe3 modifies `npm-app/release/package.json`, changing the `codebuff` package version from `1.0.507-legacy.0` to `1.0.507`. This is part of the same-day commit sequence that includes finalizing the legacy release pipeline and reverting the staging environment change.

ai.title: Codebuff legacy package bumped to 0.0.2-legacy.0
ai.summary: The version field in `npm-app/release-legacy/package.json` was incremented from `0.0.1-legacy.0` to `0.0.2-legacy.0`, continuing the legacy release sequence tracked under the `codebuff` package manifest in the `npm-app` release packaging directory. This bump follows the legacy release pipeline established in prior commits and precedes the repository rename to `CodebuffAI/codebuff`, indicating another iteration on the legacy binary distribution path.
ai.evidence: Modified file `npm-app/release-legacy/package.json`; diff shows version field changed from `0.0.1-legacy.0` to `0.0.2-legacy.0`.

eli5.text: This release updates the Codebuff tooling package to a new legacy version, which includes several improvements to how the command-line developer tool is built and how version numbers are checked for compatibility. The development script that runs the local testing setup now works more reliably across different operating systems, and environment variables needed for building the software are passed through correctly during the build process. You can now embed special configuration settings directly into the built application, giving more flexibility during setup. The version-checking logic has also been improved to better distinguish between standard and legacy releases, preventing incorrect comparisons. Upgrading to this version means you benefit from a more stable and accurate build and version management process, making local development and installation more reliable.

ai.title: Update release config to CodebuffAI/codebuff and strict semver regex
ai.summary: Release script updated to point to `CodebuffAI/codebuff` repository instead of `codebuff-community`. Version parsing regex in `npm-app/release/index.js` changed to strictly match `v` followed by `\d+\.\d+\.\d+`, replacing the previous generic tag capture and manual prefix stripping. This ensures only valid semantic version tags are accepted during the release process.

eli5.text: The release process now fetches updates from the main CodebuffAI/codebuff repository instead of the old community one, and it only accepts properly formatted version tags like v1.2.3 during publishing. This affects anyone involved in the release workflow, and youd notice that mismatched or malformed version tags will now be rejected outright rather than being silently adjusted. This change is live today as part of the release script behavior.
